title: Most bird species lacked cross-study drought records in a 2024 public release
abstract: We tested whether a public bird drought workbook supports species-response rank tests across studies. Of 204 species, 195 occur under one study ID and nine under two IDs. Only three of 378 study pairs share species. No shared species has the same response-metric label in both studies. Six abundance samples give only two pairs with shared species, each with four species in Australia. Rank correlations are -0.8 and +1.0. Exact two-sided P values are 0.333 and 0.083. Neither passes a 5% test. Four species cannot give a two-sided permutation P below 0.083. The positive-rank pair has no matching response signs. This fixed-release audit shows a limit on direct validation, not a lack of biological transfer. Source names, different methods, detection, publication selection and shared exposures limit inference. We do not test air pollution or causal climate effects. Code, full pair coverage, aggregate tests, source hashes and a figure are included.

display.caption: Shared species in six abundance samples and the two available rank comparisons. Blue lines show one-species deletion ranges, not confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Six-sample abundance scope and prior context; same biological records. New coverage and rank code.
